transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate it. 

Um... well, I hope I'm explaining this right, and I really don't want to sound, you know, crazy or anything. I'm sure it's probably just stress from work, but... I've been having a little trouble at the shop. I'm a mechanic, and lately, I keep hearing this... this man's voice. 

It comes from the garage vents, and sometimes even from under the hood when I'm working on a vehicle. It's just as clear as if somebody were standing right next to me. And, um, he keeps telling me not to trust my husband, or he tells me that I shouldn't touch certain cars. I thought it was probably best to come in and talk to someone about it. Is that... does that make sense why I'm here? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing.
How long have you been hearing this voice?

Um, well... I know I probably should have come in sooner, and I'm really sorry if I waited too long to get help. But, um... it's been about ten months now. It hasn't been forever or anything, just the last ten months. 

And... I guess, along with the voice, I've also been having these... well, these kind of silly worries that someone is tracking me? Like keeping tabs on where I go. That’s been happening for the same amount of time, about ten months. I just kept hoping it would all go away on its own if I worked harder and ignored it. Is... is it okay that I waited to come in? I really hope I'm not making things more difficult for you by waiting so long.
During these past ten months, have you experienced any long periods where your mood was extremely low or, conversely, where you felt unusually energetic, talkative, or unable to sleep?

Um... well, yes. I hope it's okay to admit this, and I really hope I haven't been too much of a bother to my coworkers or anything, but... honestly, most of this past year has been taken over by these really high-energy stretches. 

I don't want it to sound like a bad thing, because I do like being productive, but... I guess I start talking way too fast, and I take on way too much extra work at the shop. I just get to feeling so driven, almost like I can't slow down, no matter how hard I try. I really try to keep it under control so I don't overwhelm anyone, I promise. 

Is... is that the kind of thing you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and being helpful.
During these past ten months, have there been any periods where you were hearing the voice or feeling like you were being tracked, but you were NOT feeling those high-energy, driven states?

Um... yes, actually. I hope it's not bad that I'm saying this, but... yeah, there was a time. 

A little while back, I had a few weeks where things were... quieter, I guess? I wasn't running around the shop or making all those huge plans, and I was actually sleeping a lot more. Just kind of keeping my head down. But... um... I still heard the voice in the garage. And I still felt like my husband and my boss were keeping tabs on me and tracking me. 

I'm really sorry if that complicates things. I know it probably sounds confusing to have both happening, or not happening, at the same time. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.

During those weeks when you were feeling 'quieter' and sleeping more, did you also experience a period of at least two weeks where you felt deeply sad, hopeless, or lost interest in the things you usually enjoy?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I wasn't super upbeat or anything, but I definitely wasn't deeply sad or hopeless. I hope that's okay to say. 

I was just... tired, I think? Like, sleeping more, but not because I was depressed or because I didn't care about things anymore. I still liked working on the cars and everything, I just didn't have that crazy intense drive to do a million things at once. I was just taking it a little easier. 

I'm really sorry if that's not the answer you were expecting. I just want to be honest so I don't give you the wrong idea. Is it alright that I wasn't feeling sad during that time?
During those high-energy stretches you described, did you ever feel so energetic or driven that you had to stop working or go to the hospital because it was causing significant problems in your life?

Um... well... I really hate to admit this, because I always try to do a good job and be helpful, but... yes, it did cause some problems. I hope you don't think less of me, I just get so carried away sometimes. 

At the shop, I guess I was moving a little too fast and... well, I made a few mistakes. Nothing terrible, I promise! But they pulled me off the high-voltage EV work because they were worried I wasn't being safe. I felt awful about it, I really didn't mean to worry anyone. 

And then at home... my husband and I were arguing a lot because I just couldn't settle down. It got a little intense, and he actually ended up taking me in for an emergency evaluation. I know that sounds really bad, and I'm so sorry to even bring it up. I just want to be completely honest with you so you can help me. Is it okay that I told you that? I hope it's not too much.

Have you ever experienced a period of at least two weeks where you felt deeply depressed, hopeless, or had a total loss of interest in things you normally enjoy, even if it hasn't happened in the last ten months?

Um... no, I really don't think so. I hope it's okay to say that. 

I mean, I've had days where I felt a little down, like anyone else, but never for two whole weeks, and never where I felt totally hopeless or stopped caring about things. I always try to stay positive and keep busy, you know? I really love my job and working on cars, and I've never lost interest in that. 

I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Is it alright that I've never felt that way? I know you've asked about it a couple of times, and I'm really sorry if I'm not giving you the answer you need for your notes. I just want to be honest and helpful.

When you are speaking with your friends or coworkers, have they ever told you that they find it difficult to follow what you are saying, or that your thoughts seem to jump around in a way that doesn't make sense to them?

Um... well, no, not really. I mean, I hope I'm not misunderstanding the question, but people don't usually say they can't follow me. 

Sometimes when I'm really excited about a project at the shop, I guess I can talk a little fast? Like, I just have a lot of ideas all at once and I want to get them all out. But I don't think it doesn't make sense to them. They usually just kind of smile and tell me to take a breath. I always try to make sure I'm being clear, especially with the other techs. 

I'm really sorry if that's not what you were looking for. Am I making sense right now? I just want to be sure I'm answering you right.
Looking back over the entire ten months, has there ever been any time where you felt a significant, persistent period of sadness or hopelessness, even if it wasn't for two weeks straight?

Um... no, honestly, I haven't. I really hope it's okay that I keep saying no to this, I know you're trying to figure out what's going on with me. 

I mean, I really just don't get sad like that. Even when things were really stressful with my husband, or when they took me off the EV line... I felt bad that I messed up, but I wasn't, like, hopeless or crying all the time. I just wanted to fix it and do better. I always try to look on the bright side and keep moving forward. 

Is it bad that I haven't felt depressed? I'm so sorry if I'm making this difficult for you. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers so you can help me.
